agent_supports: yes (aider gates BOTH classes via io.confirm_ask — read-only "Add file to the chat?"/"Add URL to the chat?", mutating "Run shell command?"/"Allow edits to file…?")
daemon_capability: incapable (confirm_ask is a terminal stdin read; nothing marks the dialog opening in .aider.chat.history.md, the parser drops confirmation blockquotes by name, and all five waiting rules are unreachable — IdleFlush reports the blocked session as ready after 1500ms)
driver_capability: gap:permission-approval (driver hard-codes --yes-always, which aider cannot negate, and has no dialog-answer step)

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: incapable
driver_capability: gap:permission-approval

## What the scenario requires

Two DISTINCT `waiting` episodes in one session — one raised by a tool that
changes the workspace, one raised by a tool that only reads — with the arc
`ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready` and a
final `ready`. The load-bearing half is the read-only one: an integration that
subscribes to permission events for a hand-written list of dangerous tools sees
nothing for a file read or a code search, and the session stays `working` while
the user looks at a modal.

## agent_supports: yes

Aider gates BOTH tool classes, and it gates them through the same primitive —
`InputOutput.confirm_ask` (io.py:807). Every gate below is a real, separate
call site in aider 0.86.2:

MUTATING (the half `tool-gate-permission-prompt` already covers):
- `handle_shell_commands` -> `confirm_ask("Run shell command?",
  explicit_yes_required=True, group=..., allow_never=True)`
  (coders/base_coder.py:2456).
- `allowed_to_edit` -> `confirm_ask("Create new file?", subject=path)`
  (coders/base_coder.py:2207) and `confirm_ask("Allow edits to file that has
  not been added to the chat?", subject=path)` (coders/base_coder.py:2226).

READ-ONLY (the half THIS row adds):
- `check_for_file_mentions` -> `confirm_ask("Add file to the chat?",
  subject=rel_fname, group=..., allow_never=True)`
  (coders/base_coder.py:1772). This gates reading a file into the chat
  context — a pure read; nothing in the workspace changes whichever way the
  user answers.
- `check_for_urls` -> `confirm_ask("Add URL to the chat?", subject=url,
  group=..., allow_never=True)` (coders/base_coder.py:976), which on approval
  calls `cmd_web(url)` — a web fetch, also pure read.

So the row's distinguishing claim holds for aider at the AGENT layer: both
classes are gated, the gates are separate `confirm_ask` calls, and they cannot
merge into one episode because `confirm_ask` is a blocking stdin read — aider
raises them strictly one at a time. Better still for the recipe, the two
classes fire at different points of one turn cycle: `check_for_urls` runs on
the user's input before the LLM call, `check_for_file_mentions` runs on the
assistant's reply, and `handle_shell_commands` runs after edits are applied —
so a single prompt naturally produces a read-only gate and then a mutating gate
within one turn, which is exactly the shape the row asks for.

`ConfirmGroup` batches multiple items of the SAME kind (several mentioned files,
several URLs) under one remembered preference, but never merges a read-only
prompt with a mutating one — they are different `question_id` tuples
(`(question, subject)`, io.py:820) and different call sites.

## daemon_capability: incapable

The dialog leaves no trace in the Source the daemon tails, so no `waiting`
episode can be produced for EITHER class — the read-only half is not
selectively lost, the whole permission window is.

1. The transport. `Source` is `agent.FilesUnderCWD{Filename:
   ".aider.chat.history.md", Parser: agent.RawLineParser{...}}` (agent.go) —
   a markdown chat transcript, nothing else. No hooks: the aider adapter
   declares none (`Permissions` on agent.go carries only `ControlPermission`
   and the `history` observe permission; there is no `Hooks` field), so every
   hook-tier signal is unreachable by construction.

2. The QUESTION is a terminal-only stdin read; what does reach the transcript
   cannot mark either edge. This is the part most likely to be re-litigated, so
   it is spelled out. `confirm_ask` renders the question ONLY through
   `prompt_session.prompt(question)` / `input(question)` (io.py:871-895) — the
   question string itself is never written to the history file. But two other
   writes do land, and neither is usable:
   - BEFORE the block: when `subject` is set, `confirm_ask` calls
     `self.tool_output(subject, bold=True)` (io.py:850-857), and `tool_output`
     DOES append to the history as a blockquote (io.py:995-999). So a bare
     `> <filename>` / `> <command>` / `> <url>` line is written just before the
     prompt blocks. That line is indistinguishable from ordinary aider status
     output — `tool_output` is the same channel that carries the startup banner,
     `> Repo-map:`, warnings and every other status line — and it carries no
     marker saying a dialog is open. Deriving "waiting" from it would be a guess
     about prose, not the reading of a signal.
   - AFTER the answer: the `res == "d"` don't-ask-again branch writes a
     blockquote (io.py:903-905), and the `group.preference` branch echoes
     `user_input(f"{question}{res}")` (io.py:870) as a `####` line. Both are
     post-hoc, both are conditional on flags the gates in question may not set,
     and the `####` echo is read by the parser as a `user_message`, which OPENS
     a turn (-> `working`) — the opposite of the release edge.
   For gates declared without `allow_never` and without a `ConfirmGroup`
   (e.g. `confirm_ask("Create new file?", subject=path)`, base_coder.py:2207)
   NOTHING at all is written when the user answers: the release edge has no
   trace whatsoever, not merely an ambiguous one.

3. The parser cannot emit a waiting-capable event even in principle. `ParseLineRaw`
   (parser.go) emits exactly four kinds: `user_message` (`#### `),
   `assistant_message` (`> Tokens:`), `tool_result` (`> Applied edit to` ->
   Edit, `> Running` -> Bash), and `turn_done` (error blockquote or IdleFlush).
   Blockquote lines that are not errors are dropped with the comment "Other
   blockquote lines are aider status output (warnings, confirmation prompts,
   invocation echo). Ignore." — the confirmation prompt is named there
   explicitly as something the parser discards.

4. Every `waiting` rule in the classifier is unreachable for aider. The five
   rules in `stateRules` (core/application/services/state_classifier.go:106-207):
   - `SignalPermissionPrompt` (m.PermissionPending) — hook-fed; aider has no hooks.
   - `transcript_permission_prompt` (m.TranscriptPermissionPending) — fed by
     `permission.requested`/`permission.completed` transcript events (copilot);
     the aider parser emits no such kind.
   - `user_blocking_tool` (m.NeedsUserAttention) — needs an open tool named in
     `isUserBlockingToolName` (AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode, question,
     ask_user_question, exit_plan_mode, ask_user — tailer_config.go:46-54);
     aider's parser only ever names "Edit" and "Bash".
   - `SignalOpenToolStalled` ("stalled edit tool -> likely permission prompt")
     — the one transcript-tier fallback built for exactly this situation, and
     it cannot arm: aider's `toolCall()` emits `ToolUses` and `ToolResultIDs`
     in the SAME ParsedEvent, with the comment "we emit the open and close in
     one event. The state classifier sees a completed tool call without a
     permission window" (parser.go). No tool call is ever open across passes,
     so nothing can stall.
   - `SignalIdlePrompt` — hook-fed; aider has no hooks.

5. What the daemon reports instead is worse than silence. While `confirm_ask`
   blocks on stdin the transcript is QUIET, so `Parser.IdleFlush` fires after
   `aiderIdleTurnDoneAfter` (1500ms, parser.go) and synthesizes a `turn_done`,
   which the classifier's agent_done rule routes to **ready**. An aider session
   pinned behind a permission modal is affirmatively reported as FINISHED, not
   merely as still-working. That is the inversion this row exists to catch, and
   for aider it applies to both tool classes equally.

`incapable`, not `bug`. The bar for `bug` is a trace the daemon MIS-HANDLES.
Item 2 shows the transcript is not literally silent around a dialog — the
subject line is written before the block — so the question deserves a direct
answer rather than a dismissal: (a) the entry edge has no distinguishable
trace, because the subject line is emitted on the same `tool_output` channel as
every other status line and carries no marker that a dialog is open; and (b)
for gates without `allow_never`/`ConfirmGroup` the release edge has NO trace at
all, so no parser change could recover the close. A row asserting both edges
cannot be satisfied from this transport, which is `incapable`, not a defect in
how the daemon reads a signal it is given.

## driver_capability: gap:permission-approval

Two independent driver blockers, both real, the first load-bearing:

1. The interactive driver hard-codes `AIDER_ARGS=( --no-auto-commits
   --yes-always --no-gitignore )` (replaydata/agents/aider/driver-interactive.sh),
   and the recipe's `settings.aider_extra_args` can only APPEND to that array.
   `--yes-always` cannot be negated: it is declared `action="store_true"` in
   aider/args.py:760, NOT `argparse.BooleanOptionalAction` (which aider does use
   for ~30 other flags), so there is no `--no-yes-always`. With `io.yes is True`
   `confirm_ask` returns immediately without prompting (io.py:869-870 — and note
   it returns "n", a DENY, for `explicit_yes_required=True` prompts such as "Run
   shell command?"). Under the driver as it stands, neither dialog is ever
   raised; the behavior this cell asserts cannot be elicited at all.
2. There is no step type to answer a dialog. `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash
   wait_turn interrupt sleep"` (driver-interactive.sh) — the scenario's "the
   user answers the dialog (`keys`)" step has no implementation. `send` types
   literal text plus Enter and would mechanically answer a y/n prompt, so this
   is the softer of the two, but `wait_turn` counts `> Tokens:` lines and would
   have to be re-anchored around a turn that pauses mid-flight.

This is tooling, not architecture, and it is named separately from the daemon
verdict on purpose: closing it would make the cell drivable but would still
produce no `waiting` episode, because item 5 above is a transport limit.

## What would change this

Aider would have to write the permission window into `.aider.chat.history.md`
(an open marker at `confirm_ask` entry and a close at its return), or ship a
hook channel the adapter could subscribe to. Neither exists in 0.86.2. Failing
that, the daemon would need an out-of-band signal that a watched process is
blocked on a terminal read — which is not something this transport or the
current classifier can express.
caveats: VACUOUS PASS: aider CAN reach `waiting`, but only via a path that has nothing to do with a permission dialog — the trailing-question/cue text classifier (`turn ended with question or cue -> waiting`, core/application/services/state_classifier.go:437, over LastAssistantText). Because the dialog leaves no transcript trace at all, ANY `waiting` a future aider recording of this cell shows is by construction NOT the dialog. A spec asserting only "two waiting episodes appear" would go green on two question-shaped assistant replies while proving nothing.

LOAD-BEARING ENVIRONMENT PROPERTY: replaydata/agents/aider/driver-interactive.sh launches with a hard-coded `--yes-always`, which suppresses every confirm_ask dialog before it can open. A run under the current driver would observe zero dialogs for a CONFIGURATION reason, not an agent-capability one — do not let that be read back as evidence about the agent pillar.

Under `--yes-always`, `confirm_ask` returns "n" (deny) rather than "y" for prompts declared `explicit_yes_required=True` — which is the mutating "Run shell command?" gate (base_coder.py:2456). So the current driver both hides the dialog AND silently denies the mutating half.

NOT a silent transcript, and the difference matters for anyone re-litigating incapable-vs-bug: confirm_ask calls tool_output(subject) BEFORE it blocks (io.py:850-857), and tool_output appends a blockquote to .aider.chat.history.md (io.py:995-999) — so a bare `> <filename>` / `> <command>` / `> <url>` line IS written just before the dialog opens. It is still not a usable entry edge: it rides the same channel as every other status line and carries no dialog marker. The post-answer writes (the `d` blockquote at io.py:903-905, the ConfirmGroup `####` echo at io.py:870) are conditional on flags these gates may not set, and the `####` echo is parsed as a user_message (-> working). For a gate with neither allow_never nor a group — confirm_ask("Create new file?", base_coder.py:2207) — the answer writes nothing at all, so the release edge has no trace whatsoever.

daemon_capability is derived from source reading, not from a recording — no aider run of this cell exists. The claim that the session is reported `ready` while the dialog is open follows from Parser.IdleFlush's 1500ms window firing over a quiet transcript; it is a provisional emission claim in the assess sense and would be settled by a live run once the driver can raise a dialog.

sources.note: aider 0.86.2 — READ-ONLY gates: check_for_file_mentions confirm_ask("Add file to the chat?") at line 1772; check_for_urls confirm_ask("Add URL to the chat?") at line 976 (approval calls cmd_web -> web fetch). MUTATING gates: handle_shell_commands confirm_ask("Run shell command?", explicit_yes_required=True) at line 2456; allowed_to_edit confirm_ask("Create new file?") at 2207 and "Allow edits to file that has not been added to the chat?" at 2226. Anchors agent_supports: yes for BOTH tool classes.

confirm_ask at line 807: the question is rendered ONLY via prompt_session.prompt/input (871-895) and never written to the history file. tool_output(subject, bold=True) at 850-857 DOES reach the history as a blockquote via append_chat_history (tool_output, 995-999) — the closest thing to an entry trace, and still unmarked. Post-answer writes: res=='d' blockquote (903-905) and the ConfirmGroup user_input echo (870). `self.yes is True` short-circuits to "n" if explicit_yes_required else "y" (869-870). Anchors daemon_capability: incapable and the --yes-always suppression.

line 760: --yes-always is action="store_true", NOT argparse.BooleanOptionalAction (used for ~30 other aider flags) — so no --no-yes-always exists and the driver's hard-coded flag cannot be negated by appended args. Anchors driver_capability: gap:permission-approval.

ParseLineRaw emits only user_message/assistant_message/tool_result(Edit,Bash)/turn_done; non-error blockquotes are dropped with the comment naming "confirmation prompts" explicitly. toolCall() emits ToolUses and ToolResultIDs in ONE event "so the state classifier sees a completed tool call without a permission window" — which is why SignalOpenToolStalled can never arm. IdleFlush synthesizes turn_done after aiderIdleTurnDoneAfter (1500ms) over a quiet transcript.

Source = FilesUnderCWD{.aider.chat.history.md, RawLineParser}; Permissions carries only ControlPermission + the `history` observe permission and no Hooks field — every hook-tier waiting signal is unreachable for aider.

stateRules lines 106-207: the five waiting-producing rules (SignalPermissionPrompt, transcript_permission_prompt, user_blocking_tool, SignalOpenToolStalled, SignalIdlePrompt). Each is unreachable for aider — see the body's item 4. Line 437 carries the one path aider CAN reach (turn ended with question or cue -> waiting), which is the vacuous-pass hazard.
isUserBlockingToolName (lines 46-54) accepts only AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode/question/ask_user_question/exit_plan_mode/ask_user; aider's parser names only "Edit" and "Bash".

AIDER_ARGS=( --no-auto-commits --yes-always --no-gitignore ) is hard-coded; settings.aider_extra_args only appends. DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn interrupt sleep" — no keys/approval step. Anchors driver_capability: gap:permission-approval.
aider capabilities: permission_classifier "untraced" — the factory's own record that aider's permission behavior exists but leaves no trace, consistent with daemon_capability: incapable.
aider 0.86.2 options reference: --yes-always ("Always say yes to every confirmation") is the only blanket-approve flag and has no --no- counterpart documented.

recipe.notes: FROZEN on the daemon axis (daemon_capability: incapable), and separately blocked on the driver axis (gap:permission-approval). Left applicable:false with no script — same shape as the opencode/tool-gate-permission-prompt sibling — because there is no step sequence that could produce the assertion: (a) driver-interactive.sh hard-codes --yes-always and aider has no --no-yes-always (args.py:760 is action="store_true"), so no confirm_ask dialog is ever raised; (b) there is no keys/approval step to answer one; and (c) even if both were fixed, aider writes no permission-window marker into .aider.chat.history.md, and IdleFlush would report the blocked session as `ready` after 1500ms of quiet. WHAT THE RECIPE WOULD BE once (a) and (b) close: launch aider interactively WITHOUT --yes-always and with --auto-lint off; send one prompt that both mentions an un-added file by name (tripping check_for_file_mentions -> "Add file to the chat?", the READ-ONLY gate) and asks for a shell command in a ```bash block (tripping handle_shell_commands -> "Run shell command?", the MUTATING gate); answer each with a literal `y` + Enter; then hold a >=10s trailing idle. The two gates fire at different points of the turn cycle (mentions on the assistant reply, shell after edits) and confirm_ask is a blocking stdin read, so they are strictly sequential and cannot merge into one episode — the agent-layer requirement this row makes is genuinely satisfiable; only the transport is not.
preconditions: DRIVER CHANGE REQUIRED: drop the hard-coded --yes-always from AIDER_ARGS in replaydata/agents/aider/driver-interactive.sh (or make it settings-controlled). aider has no --no-yes-always to append (args.py:760 uses action="store_true"), so appended aider_extra_args cannot undo it.

DRIVER CHANGE REQUIRED: a step type that answers a TUI confirm_ask prompt (the scenario's `keys`). `send` types literal text + Enter and would mechanically answer y/n, but wait_turn counts `> Tokens:` lines and would need re-anchoring around a turn that pauses mid-flight.
DAEMON CHANGE REQUIRED (the frozen axis): aider must write the permission window into .aider.chat.history.md, or ship a hook channel. Without it no driver fix produces a waiting episode.
aider CLI on PATH with a configured provider (aider needs paid API access; the recording environment has no aider auth today).
tmux available — the interactive driver keeps the REPL alive past turn end so the waiting dwell would be observable.
